clue.text: Embryonic attachment forming lock, say

indicators.note: forming suggests the letters of the following words are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A biology note about how an embryo's attachment takes shape, likened to a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk-filled membrane hangs from a developing embryo and feeds it, a literal embryonic appendage.

clue.text: In years past, coming up for exercises

parts.note: Y is the standard abbreviation for year or years

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: past, as in 'two weeks past', means ago

explanation.surface: Someone recalling that years ago they took up some exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' applies only to the word for past, read upwards in this down light. 'In' is merely a link word here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The discipline consists of postures and breathing routines, so it is naturally described as a set of exercises.

clue.text: Troops opposed to entering field

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ley is a field left under grass
V, short for versus, means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: Soldiers advancing onto a field against an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a body of troops raised by conscription, so it can stand for troops collectively.

clue.text: Being out of step made for an ugly rush

indicators.note: being out of step signals that the letters are disordered, with step itself part of what gets jumbled

explanation.surface: A marcher falling out of step causes a messy charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A panicked headlong surge of a crowd or herd is the very picture of an ugly rush.

clue.text: Opera in 22 — sit with it (not in charge) for that in 27

annotationWithheld.why: Opera in 22 — sit with it (not in charge) for that in 27 (5): the second half is a subtractive reverse clue (sit + the answer, less IC, gives SITCOM, an alternative to soap) that the grammar cannot express
annotationWithheld.clue: Opera in 22 — sit with it (not in charge) for that in 27

clue.text: Join a firm taken in by a supposed mermaid?

indicators.note: taken in by means the following pieces sit inside the word that comes next

parts.note: to sew is to join with stitches
taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone joining a company that turns out to be run by a mermaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Manatees and dugongs are sea mammals that sailors are said to have mistaken for mermaids.

clue.text: Last year's leaders entertained by regular journalist

indicators.note: entertained by means the preceding letters are held inside the next word

parts.note: even means regular or steady

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the words Last and year's

explanation.surface: Last year's top figures being hosted by a regular reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The journalist is John Evelyn, the 17th-century diarist: a journalist in the old sense of one who keeps a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn kept a famous diary, and a diarist is literally a journal-keeper.

clue.text: Being cancelled could be to do with curses

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a cancellation was the result of a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something struck through with a line has been cancelled, as with deleted text.

clue.text: What people say about playing by ear as a tranquilliser

indicators.note: about means the outer word is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: what people say are their words

indicators.note: playing, as in improvising, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians who play by ear being told that doing so calms the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' is the anagram signal for the two words before 'ear'; 'about' wraps the speech word round the result, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of beads fingered to relieve anxiety acts as a calming device, a non-drug tranquilliser.

clue.text: Be charitable to soldier leading calf by hand

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
veal is calf meat
MS, a manuscript, is written by hand

explanation.surface: A soldier leading a calf along by hand, being kind to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Donating money or food to the poor is the classic way of being charitable.

clue.text: Director concerned with a certain type of film

parts.note: re means about or concerning
film noir is a dark style of crime film

explanation.surface: A director specialising in one particular film genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Renoir was a celebrated French film director, son of the painter.

clue.text: Depression the situation for a dog

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
the lie of something is its position or situation, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood seems the natural state for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of sheepdog originally from Scotland, so a type of dog.

clue.text: Source of 22 Bill's keeping energy by reversal of assent to MMI

parts.note: 22 is WATER BUFFALO; a source of water is a spa, a spring

indicators.note: keeping means the outer word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was William Cody, so Bill's gives Cody's
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: reversal of means the word for assent is read backwards

parts.note: yes is a word of assent

explanation.surface: A water source belonging to someone called Bill, using energy and agreeing to something in 2001.
explanation.walkthrough: MMI is 2001 in Roman numerals, and the film 2001: A Space Odyssey completes it. Bill links to 22 because Buffalo Bill was William Cody.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kubrick film title 2001: A Space Odyssey pairs the phrase with the year written in Roman numerals.

clue.text: Burglar about? Right, I speak appropriately to companion — look and see if you can help get him

definitions.text: look and see if you can help get him

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
for a cat burglar, the appropriate way to speak is to mew like a cat
at can stand for to, as in 'go at' or 'at home to'
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A burglar is lurking; you are asked to keep watch and help catch him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burglar' is there to suggest cat burglar, which makes MEW the fitting way to speak. The definition is the BBC TV series in which the public are shown crimes and asked to help catch the culprits.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC programme reconstructs crimes so viewers can watch and phone in clues to catch offenders.

clue.text: Characters in Ruddigore die off at my disposal

definitions.text: Characters in Ruddigore die off at my disposal

indicators.note: disposal means the remaining letters are arranged afresh
off means the letters of the word die are removed from Ruddigore

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan fan claiming to control the fate of the opera's characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking DIE out of RUDDIGORE leaves RUDGOR; with AT MY, 'disposal' rearranges them. The baronets of Ruddigore, the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, are the Murgatroyds, who die under a family curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ruthven and Sir Despard, baronets of the cursed family name, are leading figures in the operetta.

clue.text: Where to negotiate about listing?

parts.note: round can mean about, as in 'round the house'
a table is a list set out in columns

explanation.surface: Asking where negotiations about a list should happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Conferences of equals are held at a circular board so no one sits at the head, hence a venue for negotiating.

clue.text: Half year and half day in charge of 15

indicators.note: half here takes the second half of the word year
half here keeps only the first half of a weekday name

parts.note: Thursday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: Someone working half a year and half a day as the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'half' drops the last four letters of THURSDAY. King Arthur presided over the Round Table, entry 15.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes King Arthur the head of the knights who met at the Round Table.

clue.text: See 24
Rough patch with top off milk — no cheese to be extracted here

definitions.text: no cheese to be extracted here

indicators.note: rough suggests the following letters are roughly handled and disordered
top off means the first letter of milk is removed

explanation.surface: A rough patch of farmland where milk skimmed of its top yields no cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' strips M from MILK, leaving ILK, which joins PATCH for 'Rough' to rearrange. The definition plays on 'as different as chalk and cheese'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit dug to quarry chalk, and chalk is proverbially the opposite of cheese.

clue.text: Passport photograph makes fools dangerous

parts.note: mugs are gullible people, fools
hot can mean dangerous, as in a hot situation or hot property

explanation.surface: A passport photograph that makes people look like dangerous idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-and-shoulders police-style portrait, much like an unflattering passport picture.

clue.text: Dog suffering due to thorn

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are put through torment and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog in pain because of a thorn in its paw.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough-coated hunting breed once used to chase otters is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Monster penned by 16's father

indicators.note: penned by says that the answer, with pen written before it, makes the name, so pen is stripped from it

parts.note: 16 is ARTHUR, whose father was Uther Pendragon

explanation.surface: A monster locked up by Arthur's father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' works as PEN + the answer giving Uther PENDRAGON's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing winged reptile of legend is a classic monster.

clue.text: Type of opera in endless battle with Indian beast

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
endless means the last letter of the battle's name is dropped

parts.note: Waterloo is the 1815 battle
opera buffa is Italian comic opera

explanation.surface: A comic opera staged in an endless battle alongside an Indian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The domestic buffalo of South Asia is a beast of burden widely kept in India.

clue.text: Perplex utterly with story?

definitions.meaning: story is the American spelling of storey, a level of a building

explanation.definitionFit: A baffling question floors you, and a building's level is also a floor.

clue.text: Function of angle to disappear indefinitely

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function of an angle
to die away is to disappear

explanation.surface: An angle's function that seems to vanish without end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means adjourned without a day fixed, that is, indefinitely.

clue.text: See 19
Opening of concession requires a lot of consideration

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: thought means consideration

explanation.surface: Granting a concession calls for a great deal of reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: A concessive clause begins with words like although, so the conjunction opens a concession.

clue.text: How to receive type of opera in the bath?

definitions.text: How to receive type of opera in the bath?

parts.words: How to receive type of opera in the bath?
parts.note: a satellite dish receives television, and the kind of opera on daytime TV is the soap kind; in the bath the tray for the bar is the real sense

explanation.definitionFit: The bathroom holder for a cake of cleanser is literally a dish for that bar.

clue.text: Cover up of corporal punishment?

explanation.definitionFit: Concealing oneself is this, and a sound beating is also called this.

clue.text: Have another party in a quiet spot

definitions.meaning: to stand someone a second treat

explanation.definitionFit: A secluded hideaway is this, and treating again is the same letters read as re-treat.
